extracted.intended_audience: trademark attorneys, trademark owners/registrants, and third-party petitioners seeking to use or defend against TMA expungement/reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on requesting, instituting, and conducting ex parte expungement and reexamination cancellation proceedings under the Trademark Modernization Act of 2020, including petition content, timing, evidentiary standards, procedural steps, and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for requesting expungement proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. §2.91(b)(1), a petitioner may request an ex parte expungement proceeding in connection with a registration at any time between 3 and 10 years after the date of registration. In addition, until December 27, 2023, a petitioner may request an expungement proceeding for a registration that is at least 3 years old, regardless of the 10-year limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may also institute expungement proceedings on the Director’s own initiative within these same time periods (see 37 C.F.R. §2.92(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for requesting reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. §2.91(b)(2), a petitioner may request a reexamination proceeding in connection with a mark registered under section 1 of the Trademark Act during the first five years following the date of registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may institute reexamination proceedings on the Director’s own initiative within the same five-year period (37 C.F.R. §2.92(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may file a petition requesting institution of an expungement or reexamination proceeding. 37 C.F.R. §2.91(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one registration may be specified per petition; a petitioner seeking both expungement and reexamination for the same registration must file separate petitions for each type of proceeding (37 C.F.R. §§2.91(a), (c)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate actor for voluntary corrections vs petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination and expungement petitions are intended for third parties to bring nonuse to the USPTO's attention; a registrant whose mark was not used should not file a petition against its own registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants should voluntarily surrender the registration or amend/delete goods/services pursuant to section 7 (15 U.S.C. §1057). The USPTO previously set a $0 fee for voluntary deletions prior to a post-registration maintenance document; there is no fee for voluntary surrender (see TMEP §1608 and 37 C.F.R. §2.6 references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for an expungement petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for expungement must allege that the mark “has never been used in commerce on or in connection with some or all of the goods and/or services recited in the registration.” 37 C.F.R. §2.91(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition should identify which goods/services are alleged never used and supply evidence from the petitioner’s reasonable investigation supporting that allegation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for a reexamination petition and 'relevant date'
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for reexamination must allege that the trademark “was not in use in commerce on or in connection with some or all of the goods and/or services recited in the registration on or before the relevant date.” 37 C.F.R. §2.91(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The relevant date is defined per item: (i) for a use-based application with initial 1(a) filing (not amended to 1(b)), the filing date of the application; (ii) for an intent-to-use application under 1(b), the later of the filing date of an amendment to allege use (1(c)) identifying the goods/services or the expiration of the deadline for filing a statement of use (1(d)), including approved extensions. The relevant date is considered for each good/service identified in the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete petition form and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete petition under 37 C.F.R. §2.91(c) must be in writing, filed through TEAS, and include nine enumerated elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required elements (per 37 C.F.R. §2.91(c)): (1) fee (37 C.F.R. §2.6(a)(26), currently $400 per class); (2) U.S. registration number; (3) basis under §2.91(a); (4) name, domicile address, and email of petitioner; (5) designation of U.S. attorney if petitioner domiciled outside U.S.; (6) attorney info if represented; (7) identification of each good/service for which proceeding is requested; (8) verified statement signed by someone with firsthand knowledge that: (i) sets forth elements of the reasonable investigation (describe how/when searches were conducted and what they disclosed) and (ii) includes a concise factual statement of the basis for the petition; (9) clear, legible copies of all documentary evidence supporting a prima facie case and an itemized index. If incomplete, USPTO issues a 30-day letter to perfect limited missing elements; the 30-day response cannot add new evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable investigation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. §2.91(d), a petitioner must demonstrate a bona fide attempt to determine nonuse by conducting a reasonable investigation and include a verified statement specifying the elements of that investigation for each source relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement must describe sources searched, how and when searches were conducted, and what information/evidence the searches produced. The petition’s prima facie showing depends on the evidence gathered by this investigation and the USPTO’s registration record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'reasonable investigation'
rubrics_metrics.description: “A reasonable investigation is an appropriately comprehensive search, which may vary depending on the circumstances but is calculated to return information about the underlying inquiry from reasonably accessible sources where evidence concerning use of the mark during the relevant time period on or in connection with the relevant goods and/or services would normally be found.” 37 C.F.R. §2.91(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What is reasonable is case-by-case. Investigations should focus on the mark as disclosed, its use in the relevant marketplace, the scope of goods/services, and applicable trade channels. The investigation normally should include searches covering relevant channels of trade and advertising and consider archival evidence for past use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate sources for reasonable investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate sources include reasonably accessible sources that can be publicly disclosed (petitions will be public in TSDR). 37 C.F.R. §2.91(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested sources (non-exclusive): state and federal trademark records; internet sites/media likely owned/controlled by registrant; online media and publications where goods/services likely advertised or offered; print sources and webpages with reviews/discussions; state/federal business or regulatory filings; registrant’s marketplace activities (e.g., attempts to contact or purchase); litigation/administrative records; archived web pages (Wayback Machine®). A single internet search is likely insufficient; the investigation need not search every possible source but should produce reliable, credible evidence of nonuse for the relevant period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and notice of petition filing
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition is filed it will be uploaded to the registration record and be publicly viewable through the USPTO’s Trademark Status & Document Retrieval (TSDR) database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO will send a courtesy email notice of the petition to the registrant and/or registrant’s attorney if an email of record exists. The registrant may not respond to this courtesy notice; only responses to Office actions after institution will be accepted. Petitioners’ supporting sources should be publicly disclosable because they become part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima facie case of nonuse to institute proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: An expungement or reexamination proceeding will be instituted only for goods/services for which a prima facie case of nonuse for the relevant time frame has been established. A prima facie case requires only that a reasonable predicate concerning such nonuse be established. See 37 C.F.R. §2.92.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prima facie includes sufficient notice of the claimed nonuse to allow the registrant to respond with competent evidence. For petition-based proceedings, the determination is based on petition evidence collected via the reasonable investigation plus the USPTO registration record. For Director-initiated proceedings, the USPTO’s available information must establish a prima facie case; sources may be essentially the same as for petition-based proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution decision final and non-reviewable
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. §2.92(c)(1), any determination by the Director whether to institute an expungement or reexamination proceeding, based either on a petition or on the Director’s own initiative, is final and non-reviewable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory reference: Pub. L. 116-260, Div. Q, Tit. II, Subtit. B, §225(a), (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may consolidate proceedings involving the same registration, including a Director-initiated proceeding with a petition-initiated proceeding (37 C.F.R. §2.92(e)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple petitions concerning the same registration are submitted and no proceeding has been instituted, or the Director wishes to institute a proceeding, the Director may institute a single proceeding covering goods/services for which a prima facie case is established. Example: petitions covering goods in different classes or overlapping sets may be combined into one proceeding for efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action / Notice of institution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When a proceeding is instituted, the USPTO will issue an Office action to the registrant providing notice of the institution and requiring the registrant to provide evidence of use, information, exhibits, affidavits, or declarations reasonably necessary to rebut the prima facie case of nonuse. See 37 C.F.R. §§2.92(f)(2), 2.93(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions in these proceedings are substantively limited to the question of use in commerce. Registrants remain subject to requirements in 37 C.F.R. §2.11 (representation), §2.23 (electronic correspondence), and §2.189 (domicile address). Registrants may be required to provide domicile information and a valid email address for correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant response timing and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant must respond to the initial Office action via TEAS within three months of the issue date. Within that period the registrant may request a one-month extension of time to respond upon payment of a $125 fee (37 C.F.R. §2.93(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses must be properly signed. A timely, bona fide, substantially complete response that omits some matters may be granted 30 days (or to the end of the original response period, whichever is longer) to cure omitted items (37 C.F.R. §2.93(b)(2)). Granting additional time in such circumstances does not extend appeal or petition-to-Director deadlines. Failure to timely respond or request extension will result in termination and cancellation (see part V.F). Registrants must monitor status at least every three months until notice of termination is received (37 C.F.R. §2.23(d)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standard for registrant's proof of use
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentary evidence of use need not be the same as specimens required under Section 1(a), but must be consistent with the definition of “use in commerce” in Section 45 and relevant case law; testimonial evidence should be supported by corroborating documentary evidence. See TMEP §§901-901.03 and 37 C.F.R. §2.93.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmitting the same specimen previously submitted or a verified statement alone, without additional supporting evidence, will likely be insufficient to rebut a prima facie case. For reexamination, evidence must show use on or before the relevant date; for expungement, evidence must show use before the filing date of the petition or before Director institution. Registrants under Sections 44(e) or 66(a) may assert excusable nonuse under 37 C.F.R. §2.161(a)(6)(ii) in expungement proceedings; excusable nonuse cannot be considered for goods/services registered under Section 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deleting goods/services or surrendering registration in response
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may respond by deleting some or all goods/services at issue or surrendering the entire registration for cancellation (37 C.F.R. §2.93(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An acceptable deletion is immediately effective and may not be reinserted; no other amendments to identifications are permitted in the proceeding. If deletion occurs after filing but before acceptance of a Section 8/71 affidavit/declaration, deletion is subject to applicable fees. Filing a separate surrender or amendment request does not by itself constitute a sufficient response to an Office action—the registrant must affirmatively notify the USPTO of such a separate request in the timely Office action response. Deletions/surrenders render the proceeding moot as to those goods/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final action, appeal window, and notice of termination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant's timely response fails to establish use (or excusable nonuse where applicable) for all goods/services at issue or fails to comply with requirements, the USPTO will issue a final action (37 C.F.R. §2.93(c)(1)). The registrant has three months to file a request for reconsideration or an appeal to the TTAB; this deadline may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice of termination under 37 C.F.R. §2.94 issues if the registrant fails to timely appeal or obtain reconsideration demonstrating use or deletes remaining goods: the notice sets forth which goods/services had use established and which did not. The notice of termination is not itself reviewable on petition or appeal. If termination indicates cancellation, the USPTO will cancel the registration in whole or in part accordingly and publish cancellation in the Trademark Official Gazette; an updated registration certificate will be issued if cancelled in part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement after cancellation for failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If registration is cancelled due to failure to respond and that failure was due to an extraordinary situation, the registrant may file a petition requesting reinstatement and resumption of the proceeding under 37 C.F.R. §2.146(a)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must be filed no later than two months after actual knowledge of cancellation and not later than six months after the cancellation date in TSDR (37 C.F.R. §2.146(d)(2)(iv)). The petition must include the response to the Office action or an appeal to the TTAB (if the failure was to respond to a final action) (37 C.F.R. §2.146(c)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel consequences after termination
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon termination of an expungement proceeding in which it was established that the registered mark was used in commerce on or in connection with any goods/services prior to the date a petition was filed or Director-initiated proceedings were instituted, no further ex parte expungement proceedings may be instituted as to those particular goods/services (37 C.F.R. §2.92(d)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, reexamination proceedings (for Section 1 registrations) are not barred because reexamination asks whether use existed as of a particular relevant date. Conversely, upon termination of a reexamination proceeding establishing use on or before the relevant date, no further ex parte expungement or reexamination proceedings may be instituted as to those goods/services (37 C.F.R. §2.92(d)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-pending proceedings limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: While an expungement proceeding is pending for a registration, no later expungement proceeding may be instituted for that registration with respect to the same goods/services at issue (37 C.F.R. §2.92(d)(3)). While a reexamination proceeding is pending, no later expungement or reexamination proceeding may be instituted for the same goods/services at issue (37 C.F.R. §2.92(d)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “Same goods and/or services” refers to identical goods/services that are the subject of the pending proceeding or prior determination. Overlap does not preclude new proceedings for goods/services that are not the same; the Director may institute a proceeding for fewer than all goods/services in a petition (37 C.F.R. §2.92(c)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of USPTO action pending disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Action by the USPTO (including examination of a pending application or a TTAB proceeding) may be suspended pending disposition of an expungement or reexamination proceeding; a pending proceeding relevant to initial or continued registrability is prima facie good cause for suspension (37 C.F.R. §§2.67, 2.117(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines for examining attorneys: if ready to issue a nonfinal Section 2(d) refusal and the trademark database shows a petition or instituted proceeding, the examining attorney must issue an Office action addressing other refusals/requirements and indicate that the application will be suspended pending determination. If ready to issue a final Section 2(d) refusal, the examining attorney must suspend action pending determination. An applicant’s request for suspension (filed within the response period set in 37 C.F.R. §2.62(a)) may be considered responsive. A proceeding is not finally determined until notice of termination issued and appeal time expired; a Section 2(d) refusal cannot be withdrawn until the database shows the proceeding is terminated and any registration cancelled if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and electronic filing requirements for petitions and responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions must be filed through TEAS and include the fee required by 37 C.F.R. §2.6(a)(26) (currently $400 per class). Responses to Office actions must be filed via TEAS and be properly signed. A one-month extension to respond to the initial Office action costs $125 (37 C.F.R. §2.6(a)(27)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petitioner is domiciled outside the U.S., designation of a U.S.-qualified attorney is required (37 C.F.R. §11.14). If the petitioner must be represented, attorney contact and bar information per 37 C.F.R. §2.17(b)(3) must be provided. Petitions and associated evidence will be publicly posted to TSDR.
